Title: New Widget editor
Details: Main User Benefit : Simplify widget creation / edition thanks to a wysiwyg editor - Visual editor for the creation of widgets from scratch - Library of ready to use widgets: pop-in, banners, countdown banner... - Easy management of created widget, with a widget dashboard page - Update of the logic we associate widgets in campaigns ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/10a0c54592bc8f5924a326d97bc9e31147da4b8c17f75909f092e3168e89ddb2/10A.jpg) ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/c65d02042d0ea3d74f505f6045fac319ceb8910e6ba42ca4ecdae06e7c3ea2dc/Type_of_creation_(1).jpeg) **Hypothesis driving this project** Marketers do not see the value of our existing widget library (and to some extend our personalization module) because widgets cannot be easily customized to their needs, so we expect that solving this problem will increase the overall satisfaction of customers with our Personalization module and increase our ability to convince marketers users during sales speech. **Metric(s) and Baseline: How we will evaluate success** Baseline: number of predefined widgets used in production / month Metrics to measure when the feature is released: 1. Number of widgets created 2. NPS satisfaction measured for personalization customers (Appcues NPS for personalization customers only) 3. Win rate against AB Tasty thanks to the new widget graphic editor **Business Impact** - We expect to upsell more existing A/B testing customers to the Personalization module - We expect to increase our winning rate against A/B Tasty **Problem Statement. What pain point(s) are we trying to address?** - Today we provide a library of predefined widgets for marketers and a code-based editor to build custom widgets for developers. However, marketers can not simply create new widgets (eg. popin or banner) or adapt our existing widgets to their needs because we do not provide the right user experience or the right tools for that, so we expect that solving this problem will increase the satisfaction among our existing customers and improve our sales performance (especially when we are against AB Tasty) **How do people currently solve this problem? How do our competitors address this problem?** - They mainly ask our professional team to build custom widgets (with code) - Some competitors (Dynamic Yield or AB Tasty) provide a graphic editor or well designed widgets that can be easily customizable. **What is the project type and our justification for doing this project?** - Requested capability among SMB customers with no access to a technical team. - Some customers churned by the past to AB Tasty because they offered a more adapted product to their needs. **Jobs to be done** P0 Must have - Graphic editor for Personalization customers only - library of predefined templates that a customer can use if he does not want to start from scratch P1 Nice to have - Module that can be added as an add-on to A/B testing only customers - Ability to generate a HTML view (to embed on a mobile app as a webview). Requested by BPCE Customer) and would make sense for mobile apps customers. Dynamic Yield provides this option. - Additional components (countdown, tooltip, newsletter popin..) **When do we expect to launch?** - End of January in production - A/B testing customers only will still be able to use the existing library of widgets. So no change/update for them.

Title: Progressive Rollout
Details: ## Feature Summary Progressive \(gradual\) rollouts lets teams break up big releases into smaller chunks and remove most of the risks associated with releases by shrinking them into smaller, easier-to-control stages. Users will be able to define the features and changes you are going to release, define who they are going to be released to, when they are going to be released, and what the increments look like. --- ## Problem\/Context As a Product, Engineering or QA user, I have no way of tapering my release. I have to rely on the results of my pre-prod QA to be assured that my release will not break anything major and consequently affect all of my user base. I am also unable to plan for any sudden loads on bandwidth, storage or infrastructure when my new release is made public. - **Existing workaround:** None. Currently, users would have to create individual rollouts for each individual increment. - **Justification:** A major selling point for some of our competitors. Progressive rollouts are an established good practice and meets our audience's needs. --- ## Solution - **Product package:** Full stack - **User roles**: PM, EM, QA, RM - or anyone concerned with product\/version releases. - **Product scope:** The option can be found in the right overlay when adding a new rule in the Rollout Planner. All UI changes reside in the same overlay. - **Product design:** Selecting this option will prompt the user to define a few parameters: 1. Choose Progressive rollout when adding a new rule ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/b019216e125aaf2aa9da9f80bc8f02128c11b7c2c3f91fb6ffdbddddbcb6b1c5/image.png) Then, in the next screen, fill in your parameters for progressive rollout: 1. Choose audience\/segment for this rule \(or create a new one\) 1. Start date 1. Initial exposure \(e.g: 0%\) 1. Increment \(e.g: 20%\) 1. Interval between increments \(e.g: 5 days\) 1. Final exposure cap \(e.g: 80%\) Upon this final entry, the user sees an indication of when and at what exposure percentage the rollout will stop. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/27fcda0472191b50264f4291e43a0b11159bf9fe4e8a84fa925327d9b464a06b/image.png) --- ## **Measuring Success** - **Market-Fit:** This feature brings us on par with LaunchDarkly and Flagship, the only two competitors offering this functionality. - **Adoption:** Once released, active customers try out progressive delivery at least once. --- ##

Title: Sample ratio mismatch
Details: This feature would be a flag which would be raise if we detect that the statistical results we show might not be valid because the observed deviation between the reference and the variations are not what should be expected. One can read about it [here](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/experimentation-platform-exp/articles/diagnosing-sample-ratio-mismatch-in-a-b-testing/). Implementation wise it would be to a use a test such as a chi-square statistic to determine whether the observed distribution of users in experiment variants statistically differs from the one that was configured. To compute it we need the number of visits in the reference and in each variation and the expected deviation for this experiment. If the difference is significative p-value \< 0.0005) we raise the warning. Requested by Zalora

Title: Multiple testing correction method
Details: This correction helps against the [multiple comparisons problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_comparisons_problem) basically, as we increase the number of variation, we increase the number of test statistics being computed and doing so, we increase the probability of being wrong. Saying otherwise, as we add more variation, it becomes increasingly likely that one variation appears as a reliable winner due to random sampling error alone. To shield our customer from taking wrong conclusion we should implement a correction to the displayed reliability in case of multi-variate testing \(it could be extended to goals in a second time\). A first very simple correction would be the Bonferroni one, where we simply multiply the p-value by the number of variations. A preferred and more advanced one would be the Holm-Bonferroni one. It requires to first sort all the p-values of the tests, and then to multiply the smallest by the number of variations, the second smallest by the number of variation minus one etc. If one wants to use multi-variate testing than this is crucial - since only a few of our customers have the traffic to use multi-variate testing it might not have the biggest added value.Since we are focusing on ENTERPRISE and these should have more traffic it might be interesting as well for normal testing when there are 3,4,5 variants only

Title: Contentful Integration
Details: ## **Feature short Describe what the feature does. The Contentful Integration allows Contentful users to run experiments on content directly from Contentful UI and use Kameleoon powerful analytics solution to analyse the performance of those experiments. **What is Contentful ?** Contentful is a headless CMS, a composable content platform that meets the unique demands of digital content and all the teams that produce and work with it. Built with an API-first architecture, Contentful orchestrates content from multiple sources and publishes it to any digital channel. It ensures content is discoverable and reusable, provides tailored interfaces, and incorporates governance through role-based access management and workflows. **What is a Headless content management system \(CMS\) ?** A headless CMS comprises three parts: a backend, APIs, and an interface. The backend stores content and organizes data. [ APIs ](https://www.contentful.com/blog/2015/10/22/contentful-a-content-platform/) connect the database to presentation layers. These presentation layers are independent from the CMS and thus malleable. Headless CMSes are defined by this lack of presentation layer. \(If you were looking for it, this is the head in headless CMS.\) Going headless allows you to distribute content through multiple channels on all sorts of platforms at scale. ## Problem What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? As a Contentful user, I would like to have Contentful as the single source of truth when creating content for the different projects I manage (website, mobile app, etc). When I want to create an experiment with a version B on a Contentful content, I cannot do it in Contenful, I have to use Kameleoon graphic editor which is not convenient. I'd prefer to run experiments on content using the Contentful UI and use Kameleoon to analyse the performance on my experiment. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround asking a developer to use Contentful API in a coded experiment in Kameleoon. ## Solution **Key benefits** : What value does this feature bring to the user? Bringing experimentation capabilities to Contentful for users in charge of managing the website content through Contentful CMS Keep Contentful as the single source of truth for your content. Run advanced no-code experiments on structured content (copy, components, layouts and pages) managed in Contentful Reduce the amount of manual work needed and get the best of both world: managing variants of an experiment in Contentful, benefiting from Kameleoon powerful experimentation engine and analytics solution Marketers don't have to be dependent on developers to lead experimentation No flicker: benefiting from server side instant bucketing by serving variations with no latency **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users. Run any experiments based on content (copy, components, layouts and pages) defined in Contentful and benefit from the best of both worlds. ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Full Stack Experimentation \/ Feature Management - **Product scope:** It's all on Contentful side \(you have to install the Kameleoon app from their marketplace\) - **Target Persona**: Users in charge of the content and willing to run experiments \(Marketer in charge of the CMS\) - **Main updates:** The Kameleoon app allows users to quickly and easily populate content \(e.g., CTAs, forms, posts\) from Contentful into each variation of a Kameleoon experiment. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/26a6265a91316a73e6d572d879028d78ecdd73644fdd7a7c355d6edcabcae243/image.png) Installing this app will create a new content type called Kameleoon Container which will read your projects, experiments, and variations from Kameleoon. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/29ff342f5e90114a26709c74d538284c4c2ae3297a8b33fc6b865ed088519f76/image.png) Users can finalize the content of their variations in Contentful, then launch their experiments and track ## **Measuring Success** NA --- ##

Title: Components to easily reuse any element anywhere
Details: **Use case :** It can be very useful to reuse a same element either in the same widget (in the same screen or on other screens) or even in other widgets. For example, if you create a multi screens widget, you might need to reuse a same button on each screen. **Solution proposed:** - From any screen of the "Design Tab", you can select any element and "Create a component" (clicking on the 3 dots icon) - Then, in the "Add element" section (on click on + icon), a new section "Components" appears, with the list of all components already defined. Choose on component of the section to add it to the screen being editied. - Later, if you decide to edit this component to update its design, all the changes will be applied for each instance of the component (in other words, you update the component only once, and the changes apply wherever the component is used) - If you want to apply a change only for a specific instance, you will be able to "Detach instance" (to make it independant from the component) This "Component" feature can save designers a lot of time when creating their screens. . Nice many elements on websites are standard ones, like buttons - they always the same. It is crucial to be able to re-use once defined elements. When duplicating elements (buttons) or wanting to duplicate the same desing but for different text.Confirmation popin (you want the same size and background) / Also asked by Quest Diagnostics (US brand). Title: Login spaces
Details: # **User Story** As a user not authenticated, I want to authenticate with a copy/paste of my email containing spaces (before or after the email address) so that I can authenticate to the app without errors because of the spaces in the email. # **Tickets** # **Summary** Detect and delete spaces before and after the email address in the login page to avoid errors. # **Functional specifications** ## Use cases It will reduce copy and paste problems on our and customers side. ## Functional scope *Where will this feature be used?* The login page only. ## Expected behaviors & Diagrams If the user enter an email with a space **before or after** it, those spaces will not be considered as being a part of the email and will be automatically deleted after submission. Exemple: "test@email.com" + "password" = OK then " [test@email.com](mailto:test@email.com)" + "password" = also OK and "[test@email.com](mailto:test@email.com) " + "password" = also OK too ## Errors The email (without the spaces before and after it) need to match the associated password, otherwise a classic error will be displayed, just like it is right now. # **Technical specifications** ## Risk assessment The login page is very critical for the app and any modification on it need to be deeply tested before deployment. # **Wireframes & Mockups** The interface stays the same. We need to see if this feature can be replaced by another behavior. Using VS Code + Git is still a cleaner way to keep track of the different versions. So maybe we can build a Git integration that will be used within the Code Editor. Git server usually have that API that allows us to do it. # Solution **Package** A/B Testing / Personalization / Full stack **Scope** Code Editor and GS page **User roles** Technical ***Design** Need to be done # **Measuring Success** **Goal 1** Measure the use of code versioning among our users. **Success metric** Number of users/customers that are using code versioning **Success metric** Number of experiments that are using code versioning --- # Attached documents **Figma file**: optional (paste link) **Spec file**: optional (paste link) **Redmine ticket**: mandatory (paste link) Code versioning (Code editor and GS):Today, if a change is made, the previous version of code is lost.It would be very practical to offer the clients the possibility of saving the code and then getting it back from the history created. Title: Targeted Delivery

This means it's impossible to be selective with feature and who can access them. Planning releases around user attributes such as geographical location, type of subscription, device\/platform, and any other use case involving advanced segmentation is currently not possible. - **Existing workaround:** None. - **Justification:** A huge value-add for our product, similar to how Custom Data opens up advanced possibilities for our A\/B testing product. Paired with the new rollout planner, this feature effectively also allows staged deliveries to be executed. --- ## Solution - **Product package:** Full stack - **User roles**: PM, EM, QA, RM - or anyone concerned with product\/version releases. - **Product scope:** The option can be found in the right overlay when adding a new rule in the Rollout Planner. All UI changes reside in the same overlay. - **Product design:** Selecting this option will prompt the user to define a few parameters: 1. Choose Targeted Delivery when adding a new rule ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/e63f4530761a059825ee20bdf1f5248d7358e6f4c4c2ef66505e4f7696a29520/image.png) 1. Choose audience\/segment for this rule \(or create a new one\) 1. Define the exposure rate for your segment 1. Title: Hybrid Capability: 3P Analytics Tools
Details: ## **Feature short Allows users to use integrations with 3P Analytics platforms \(e.g. Mixpanel, GA...\) and export results of delivery and experiment rules to analyze outside Kameleoon. ## Problem Today, Hybrid capabilities don't extend to FME and is a deal-breaker for customers whose users are already using an analytics platform and would like to keep reporting streamlined within it. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** No ## Solution **Key benefits** : - With hybrid experimentation, developers do not need to configure code for analytics tracking or set up third-party integrations. Once the PM configures the feature experiment or delivery rule, anyone can iterate on and analyze it. Analysts or PMs can activate data derived from the feature flag with relying on the developer. - Customers can continue to use their preferred analytics tools without any breaks in the UX. - For cost-saving flexibility, users can customize **per flag** whether to track delivery rules, experiments, or both. - Absolutely market-competitive feature ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/6350f1c1437e9b777a1f2e918dc0eed4281ba2d760e134a23e47cb954f8c66fa/image.png) ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management & Experimentation - **Product scope:** Rollout Planner \(but affects entire FME offering\) - **Target Persona**: PM, Developer, Analyst - **Main updates:** - An additional menu item under the **Reporting** section - On clicking, user sees all of the \(globally\) existing integrations associated with the account - Optionally, users can toggle whether to track data for delivery rules, experiment rules, or both ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** Get more integration facilitation for fullstack customers - **Success metric:** Number of integrations used \/ flag --- ##

Title: Engine last rebuild date in app
Details: # Problem\/Context ## **Description** When users are doing changes in production, a request is sent to start rebuilding the kameleoon.js script, to update the CDN with the last version of kameleoon.js. The problem is that users can't see anything from this process. They don't know if the process started or if script has finished rebuilding. So the goal here is to provide the user more information like the "last rebuild done" so they will know if their script is updated. We are now displaying the last rebuild date in the project page. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/4efbf77c0b5f4f35cf30eb56a76087be63320bf4f1ec7c74b80275d39e9b8c9f/image.png) ## Workaround No. ## **Project justification** **Project type** - Requested capability **Justification** I think customers are complaining about this, or at least it can help our consultants in providing a better support to our customers. # Solution **Package** A\/B Testing \/ Personalization **Scope** To be defined **User roles** All **Design** To be defined # **Measuring Success** To be defined --- # Attached documents **Figma file**: optional \(paste link\) **Spec file**: optional \(paste link\) **Redmine ticket**: Engine - Sending queue messages: For the engine part, we have two options: - Option 1 : The rebuild is successful \(we have a success status\), then we send a message in the queue \( queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms \) containing the sitecode. This is what we are currently doing : we send a message \( through queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms \) to notify the CDN to purge the cache. This action is triggered when the rebuild is successful. - Option 2 : The rebuild respond with an OK\/KO status, then the engine will create a new queue \(like queue-kameleoon-rebuild-status \) and send an object containing the sitecode and the status. This is what we can do if we would like to send a status with the sitecode, so this queue will be triggered whether the rebuild is successful or not \(compare to the queue-kameleoon-js-file-ms queue that is triggered only when the rebuild is successful, this is why there's no status in it\). Backend - Saving queue objects in the database: On the backend side, we wait for the queue objects, and save them using the sitecode associated with the data as an array containing the date \(or the status in the case of option 2\). Done the same time as ADMIN Back-office. Title: Forced SDK Decision method for testing and debugging
Details: **Overview:** The Forced SDK Decision feature empowers developers to test and debug various application flows by overriding standard variation assignment. It will allow developers to force specific users into predetermined variations, helping with experiment setup and debugging processes without using the Kameleoon app. **Key Benefits:** - **Controlled Testing:** Precisely manage which variation users experience, ideal for troubleshooting and validating experiments. - **Enhanced Debugging:** Simplify debugging by forcing decisions at the SDK level, allowing quick identification of potential issues. - **Customizable Flow:** Modify or remove forced decisions as needed, ensuring flexibility during testing. **Use Cases:** - Validating experiment setup before full rollout. - Debugging user flows in development or production environments. - Isolating specific variations for testing with specific user groups. Possibility to Q/A feature flags by forcing the display of a variation- Using a command in the console- Through the Kameleoon extension It will help us immensely in the QA process of tests Te easy verify the different versions, without clearing cookies, pausing the test, or changing in the experiment When we develop new functionality, we often have requirements to "hide" new functionality behind an A/B test. This makes it hard to test new functionality since we may get the "staus quo" version when testing. Thus, we can't see if the new functionality works. To simplify testing of A/B test during stageing We neee to be able to do QA on feature flags Developers can have direct control over which variations are shown to which users, and can expect a more streamlined way to validate your setup and configurations in real-time. makes it easier to see the outcome of an Ab test would help us a lot at various clients especially for our developers inconvenient to use the kameleoon site to do this We are currently working with multiple environments and have a lot of A/B tests running at the same time. Often tests overlap and we need to force a variation of one test in order to test something else. We need this to showcase to our stakeholders when we do major changes that they might become aware of from our customers, as the tests can potentially affect our customer experience significantly negatively. Also for our quality assurance, it eases the work significantly as we are ramping up experimentation significantly. Q/A-testing of A/B-test would be much easier to perform So that we can more easily present variations of an A/B test to our stakeholders. Our cro expert needs it For QA purposes

Details: ## Feature Summary **Activity Logs** will effectively maintain a track of all Kameleoon user activities pertaining to Feature Flags that happened within a customer's account. In high-stakes environments, logs are critical to be able to trace your steps back for debugging, potential rollbacks or identifying incorrect targeting conditions. 1. **Transparent workflow management:** When experimentation, feature flags or delivery management have several stakeholders involved, not having a clear way to uphold accountability for actions can lead to problems and uncomfortable situations. Logging ensures each action performed on Kameleoon can be linked back to individual users and thus ensure sanctity of daily operations 1. **Monitoring & Compliance:** Given the substantial overlap of DevOps with feature flagging, logs help find needles in a haystack, and subsequently make the software delivery cycle more secure and compliant 1. **Tech. Debt Management:** A major challenge of working with feature flagging is the tech debt that accumulates over time. Logs also help weed out flags that have become obsolete or orphaned. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/65e172ac15722631480c4d95145f78af3286712c2398c13a0e166b526bd10904/image.png) ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management and Experiment - **Product scope:** Rollout Planner - **Target Persona**: PM, Developer - **Main updates:** An additional menu item under the **Reporting** section, with a similar activity log as the main platform \(\+ filters adapted to the reported changes\) ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** Drive more value for larger teams interested in this feature - **Success metric:** Feature adoption --- ##

Title: Automatic Rollbacks
Details: ## **Feature short This feature will allow users of FME to turn off a feature automatically if predefined KPI thresholds are met. The user will be able to choose the KPIs that will act as triggers for the rollback, as well as the values at which the feature should turn off. The user can also choose the minimum number of visitors evaluated or time elapsed before the rollback condition takes effect, as well as the option to notify themselves or others if a rollback occurs. ## Problem - As a PM, dev or analyst, when I want to proactively turn off a poorly performing feature with minimal monitoring, theres no way to set and forget. - Even Progressive delivery rules, despite their slow ramp-up, still need to be monitored manually. - Implementing automatic feature rollbacks can be complex and time-consuming, requiring significant effort to set up and maintain - I dont have control over critical mass of customers to have been exposed before my guardrail takes action \(to ensure the rollback is not a false positive\) - I have to configure alerts from the results page and can only do so for experiments at the moment - and the entire process is very disjoint from the creation step. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Partially - **Workaround Only for Feature Experiments Using the results page of experiments to create manual alerts for specific KPIs. ## Solution **Key benefits**: 1. **Saves time and effort:** Automatic feature rollbacks save developers time and effort by automatically rolling back features that are causing issues or bugs, rather than having to manually identify and revert them. 1. **Reduces downtime:** By quickly detecting and rolling back problematic features, automatic feature rollbacks can help reduce system downtime and minimize the impact on end-users. 1. **Improves stability:** By automatically detecting and rolling back problematic features, the overall stability of the system can be improved, reducing the likelihood of future issues. ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management - **Product scope:** Inside rule configuration overlay - **Target Persona**: All - **Main updates:** - Additional step when creating or editing a rule. - User selects parameters for triggering rollback and the minimum thresholds. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/6d814765e3f1aaef1f4cf71292df26958e3e326bf6d4317e2381bb4197b91ba9/image.png) ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** Feature adoption - **Success metric:** No. of rollbacks configured --- ##

Title: Cross campaign analysis
Details: The Cross campaign analysis feature allows users to filter/breakdown the data on the result page by "Campaign", to analyze the impact of a campaign on another. ## Problem What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? When analyzing the results of a campaign, a user is not currently able to know the effects of a campaign on another, which would bring a lot of insights as a visitor might have been subject to multiple campaigns, affecting his behavior. It will give more transparency to data analysis on Kameleoon. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** No ## Solution **Key benefits** : What value does this feature bring to the user? -Allow deeper analysis -Knowing if a visitor has seen multiple campaigns and not only the one of the result page the user is on -Knowing what impact the combination of multiple campaigns might have had on visitors **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users. I have 3 campaigns running on my website, and I don't understand why my results seem off. I will breakdown my results by campaign to check if it might be the combination of my campaigns that have a certain effect on visitors, as it could just be one of my campaign that is bringing the others down. I can breakdown and filter by campaign but also by a specific variation of a campaign. ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation \/ Full Stack Experimentation \/ Feature Management \/ AI-driven Personalization - **Product scope:** Experiments and Personalizations Result pages - **Target Persona**: Marketer \/ Product Manager - **Main updates:** - On the result page of a campaign, I click on breakdown\/filter and select "campaign" - I choose which perso\/experiment or variation I want to filter\/breakdown on and validate - Filter : The filter will be applied and appear in "Filter by", and the results will be filtered by the chosen campaigns. - Breakdown : The breakdown will be applied and the details of every variation will appear ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** More depth - **Success metric:** The number of times this filter\/breakdown is used on result pages. --- ##

Title: Raw visit/visitor export
Details: ## **Feature short Describe what the feature does. Raw visit/visitor export allows every user to get the raw data of an experiment by adding the option to export the data "raw" in the "export" menu in the "Actions" dropdown, on the result page. ## Problem What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? As a user, I can't currently get the data Kameleoon is collecting in order to display the result page, and can only get the data showing on the result page. I would like to get the raw data of an experiment when I'm on a result page, to be able to analyze it with my own tools for example. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround : Users can specifically ask Kameleoon to access the raw data of an experiment, and we can provide them such data, because we do have it, we just didn't make it available to everyone easily yet. ## Solution **Key benefits** : What value does this feature bring to the user? -It brings more transparency to the users, as they can see the data we are getting on their website before we transform it and display it on the result page. -It will give more flexibility to users as they will be able to manipulate the data on their end, and they might want insights we don't currently offer on the result page. **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users. When user wants to analyze data of an experiment run on their website, as they love Kameleoon experiments but rather experiment with their data themselves, they will be able to get this data and do whatever they want with it. ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation \/ Full Stack Experimentation \/ Feature Management \/ AI-driven Personalization - **Product scope:** Product section and pages that will evolve \(if needed, define sections\/pages that will be out of scope\) - **Target Persona**: Which one of our target persona is going to benefit from this feature? \(Marketer \/ Developer \/ Product Manager\) - **Main updates:** - In the result page \>\> in the actions dropdown \>\> in the export section - There will be a new field, above all the others, called " type of export", with 2 options : raw \(new\) or aggregated data \(what we currently offer\) - If aggregated is selected, nothing changes, it stays the same as it is now - If raw is selected, we remove the last 2 fields \("include" , and "view by goal"\) and add a new field called "email address", where the default email will be the account one, but the user can edit this field and type his own mail if it's not the same \( as many users can use the same account \) - User validates and receives, when it's ready, either the file with the format he selected, or a link to download the file \( we're not sure yet about what's the best\) - We have not decided of a time\/size limit yet, but we might add one if needed. ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** The goal of this topic is to add more transparency and flexibility in the analysis capacity we offer to our customers - **Success metric:** The key metric indicator will be the number of raw exports done across our customers' accounts --- ##

Title: Bot Filtering for Full Stack Experimentation
Details: Websites today are commonly visited by **bots** and **spiders** which skew event tracking and conversion data by posing as actual human visitors. Experiment results can lose their value if numbers get inflated due to bot visits, which is why Kameleoon provides an easy solution for Full Stack customers to filter out bots with known [user agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_agent) that are listed on the actively maintained [**IAB\/ABC**](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/iab-abc-international-spiders-bots-list/) database. > *The IAB has enlisted The Alliance for Audited Media to perform evaluation and management services associated with maintaining and publishing the industry Spider and Robot list, the use of which is required for compliance to the IABs Client Side Counting \(CSC\) Measurement Guidelines for double pass filtering.* When tracking events with an SDK, Full Stack customers will need to simply pass their visitors' *user agent* attribute along with the other information for the bot to automatically be filtered.

Title: Edge CDN Kits
Details: ## **Feature summary:** An Edge CDN is cloud technology that specializes in static site hosting and serverless functions. It provides developers with a seamless way to deploy and scale their websites, web applications, and APIs. They focus on simplifying the deployment process and optimising the performance of web projects - ensuring fast loading times and efficient delivery to end users. --- ## Solution benefits What value does this feature bring to the user? - **Improved website performance:** Edge CDN technologies distribute content closer to end users, reducing latency and improving website loading speeds. This results in a better user experience and higher engagement levels. - **Reduced bandwidth costs:** By caching content at edge server locations, edge CDNs help offload traffic from origin servers, reducing the bandwidth consumption and associated costs. - **Enhanced scalability:** Edge CDNs offer scalable infrastructure that can handle high volumes of traffic without impacting performance. This enables websites to accommodate sudden spikes in user activity or handle increased demand during peak periods. - **Increased global reach:** With edge server locations distributed across the globe, edge CDNs can deliver content to users regardless of their geographical location. This improves website accessibility and ensures consistent performance for users worldwide. - **Improved reliability and resilience:** Edge CDNs use a distributed network of servers, reducing the risk of single points of failure. If one edge server goes down, requests can be automatically rerouted to the nearest available server, ensuring continuous content delivery. - **Flexibility and agility:** Edge CDNs provide flexibility in managing and delivering content. Title: Multi-Armed Bandit Experiments
Details: ## Feature Summary The goal of this feature is to introduce a **Multi-Armed Bandit** for traffic allocation in Feature Experiment's variation split. The MAB will optimize the distribution of user traffic among different feature variations, allowing for efficient and automated decision-making during A\/B testing and experimentation. --- ## Problem - As a user, I face: - **Inefficient Traffic Allocation:** Challenges in determining the optimal allocation of user traffic among multiple feature variations during A\/B testing. Manual allocation methods may result in suboptimal decisions and wasted opportunities. - **Missed Opportunities:** Manual allocation, especially over several ongoing experiments may fail to leverage real-time feedback from ongoing experiments, leading to missed opportunities to quickly identify and promote high-performing variations. - **Resource Drain:** Manual management of traffic allocation requires significant time and effort from me and my team, diverting their focus away from core tasks and slowing down the experimentation process. - **Workaround:** None, manual intervention is a must. ## Solution Benefits 1. **Optimized Traffic Allocation:** Intelligently adjusts the distribution of user traffic among different feature variations based on real-time feedback. It dynamically balances exploration \(trying out new variations\) and exploitation \(promoting successful variations\), leading to better overall performance and quicker identification of winning variations. 1. **Quick Insights and Iteration:** Users can gain actionable insights more rapidly, allowing users to iterate and improve their products faster. 1. **Resource Efficiency:** Eliminates the need for manual management, saving users time and effort. Users can focus on strategic decision-making and experiment analysis rather than manual allocation. ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/64ecaa5e8e1753c337fe0c639ccb05ccba2251d9d76e75d1b7b2877cb1fafd6a/image.png) ![](https://pb-files.s3.amazonaws.com/production/attachments/bd0f1c481e68fd13803977e89a4126be9d7b16f69caa3b5a7fe5b642f793efb6/image.png) ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Feature Management and Experiment - **Product scope:** Rollout Planner - **Target Persona**: PM - **Main updates:** A simple toggle in the experiment variation split selection. ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** Improved conversion metrics - **Success metric:** Feature adoption, user feedback --- ##

Title: Sequential testing
Details: ## **Feature short Describe what the feature does. Sequential Testing allows users to continuously monitor the performance of different variations in an A/B test and make informed decisions as soon as statistically significant results are achieved, without the need to wait for a fixed sample size to be reached. ## Problem What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? Traditional A/B testing methods often require a predetermined sample size and fixed testing duration, which can lead to inefficiencies and delayed decision-making. In many cases, users are left waiting for extended periods before they can confidently choose a winning variation or halt underperforming ones. This approach is suboptimal in scenarios where quick decisions are essential, such as optimizing conversion rates, user engagement, or revenue generation. Sequential Testing aims to address these limitations and provide a more flexible and efficient testing framework. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround : Users can manually check his experiment's results on all the existing segments to see the test's result on each. ## Solution **Key benefits** : What value does this feature bring to the user? -Faster Decision-Making: Sequential Testing enables users to make decisions as soon as statistically significant differences between variations emerge, reducing the time required to reach conclusive results. -Resource Efficiency: Users can optimize their testing resources by stopping underperforming variations early and reallocating traffic to more promising ones, leading to cost savings and better allocation of resources. -Improved User Experience: By quickly identifying and implementing winning variations, organizations can enhance user experience, drive better engagement, and ultimately improve key performance metrics. -Adaptive Testing: The feature adapts to the actual behavior of users, ensuring that if a significant difference exists, it will be detected with high probability while minimizing the risk of making incorrect decisions due to random fluctuations. **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users. This feature can be used for each AB test. ** Product design:** - **Product package:** All packages. - **Product scope:** Result page. - **Target Persona**: Marketer \/ Product Manager - **Main updates:** - Addition of a toggle to choose between sequential or classic approach. ## **Measuring Success** - **Goal 1:** The goal is to align with our competitors who offer this feature. - **Success metric:** Number of customer running a sequential experiment. --- ##

Lack of Accountability: When changes to feature flags are made by a single individual, it becomes difficult to trace back and assign responsibility in case of errors or negative outcomes. 1. Compliance and Governance: Organizations operating in regulated industries or following strict compliance requirements may face difficulties in meeting audit and governance standards without a robust approval process in place. Gains: 1. Enhanced Security: By requiring the involvement of multiple authorized individuals, the Four-Eyes Principle adds an extra layer of security, reducing the risk of unauthorized or malicious changes to feature flags. 1. Improved Quality Control: Having multiple reviewers ensures that proposed changes undergo thorough scrutiny, catching errors, inconsistencies, or potential pitfalls early in the process, leading to higher-quality software deployments. 1. Shared Knowledge and Collaboration: The Four-Eyes Principle fosters collaboration and knowledge sharing among team members. Reviewers can provide valuable insights, suggestions, or alternative approaches to improve the feature flag configurations. 1. Transparent Decision-Making: With a clear approval workflow and audit trail, the decision-making process becomes transparent and accountable, enabling stakeholders to understand who reviewed and approved each change. 1. Compliance and Auditing: Organizations can meet regulatory and compliance requirements by having a controlled and documented approval process for feature flag changes, ensuring accountability and adherence to established guidelines. 1. Confidence in Deployments: By implementing the Four-Eyes Principle, users of the feature flag tool can gain confidence in their deployment process, knowing that changes are subject to thorough review and scrutiny, reducing the risk of negative impacts on end-users. 1. Error Detection and Prevention: Multiple sets of eyes can identify potential issues, such as conflicts with existing feature flags, incorrect configurations, or unintended consequences, minimizing the chances of introducing bugs or performance regressions. 1. Continuous Improvement: The feedback and suggestions provided by the reviewers during the approval process can lead to iterative improvements in feature flag configurations, resulting in a more optimized and stable software system over time. By embedding the Four-Eyes Principle into the workflow of a feature flag tool, users can benefit from increased security, improved quality control, collaborative decision-making, and better compliance with industry standards. Nice to keep a clean dashboard A common issue for users is Back-office "cluttering", primarily involving segments and goals, but also experiments. It would be great to highlight to the user when creating a new segment that the one theyre trying to save already existsthis would prevent the problem of duplicating identical segments. The same applies to goals, though Im not sure if such a check is feasible.

Title: Experiment-Level Global Code
Details: ## **Feature short Describe what the feature does. This feature allows Developers to easily incorporate and manage experiment-specific global code directly within the experiment. By providing a dedicated global code field, it enables the simulation of global scripts and facilitates the inclusion of temporary code for targeting purposes. The added benefit of automatic code removal upon experiment stopping ensures a clean and efficient process, contributing to overall performance optimization. ## Problem What problem are we trying to solve with this feature? Or, what is the opportunity we are addressing? As a developer, when I want to implement experiment-specific global scripts or include temporary code for precise targeting in experiments, I encounter the following problems: Lack of a dedicated space within each experiment for global code management that only serves that experiment. The only way is to add that code to the global tracking script which has several drawbacks : - no possibility to simulate that code, - cluttered and less organized setup as the global script contains both temporary experiment code and tracking code for goals conversions..), resulting in potential performance issues and a lack of code cleanliness. **Workaround:** - **Existing workaround:** Yes - **Workaround adding that code to the Global Tracking Script ## Solution **Key benefits** : What value does this feature bring to the user? This feature streamlines the development process by providing a dedicated space for experiment-specific global code. Developers can now confidently implement and test code within the scope of each experiment, minimizing the risk of introducing bugs into the production environment. The separation of experiment code from the global tracking script eliminates the need for risky workarounds, contributing to a smoother and more reliable development experience. **Use Cases:** Share use cases where this feature would help our users. When the developer wants to add temporary code (e.g., for targeting purposes), they want to seamlessly integrate and execute that code within the experiment setup, ensuring it is processed by Kameleoon before any targeting takes place. This enables developers to efficiently include temporary code for targeting purposes directly within the experiment, ensuring it gets executed by Kameleoon at the appropriate stage. This streamlines the development process and ensures precise targeting without compromising on the organization and execution of the code. ** Product design:** - **Product package:** Web Experimentation - **Product scope:** Code Editor - **Target Persona**: Developers ## **Measuring Success** **Feature Adoption Rate:** - We will measure how quickly users adopt the new feature. A high adoption rate may indicate that the feature is well-received and addresses user needs. **Performance improvements:** - Evaluate the cleanliness and organization of code by measuring the reduction of code within the global tracking script. Measure what's the average size of the global script today versus in about 1-3 months after the feature is released. --- ##

Title: CUPED : configuration possibilities
Details: # Implementation Notes \(Microsoft 2013\) - In general, the optimal pre-experiment window is 12 weeks. A shorter window doesnt capture enough variance and a longer window captures noise. - For longer experiments, a longer pre-experiment window is needed to ensure that the same users are observed both during and prior to the experiment. - CUPED performance is highly dependent on the metric; a metric with high variance across the user population will perform well. - Make sure you that your covariate *X* will be evenly distributed between treatment and control. If its systematically impacted by a treatment, CUPED becomes invalid. - The CUPED method above only removes variance that can be accounted for linearly. Non-linear methods will be discussed in future posts. Today the value seems to be 2 weeks and it is not configurable,. Would be great to have the possibility to configure it

Title: Scheduled XML file import
Details: Be able to set a specific time for the import of XML files in the product recommendations module.Then we will know that our latest updates always get included. Minimize errors in the product recommendations feed. We currently risk having faulty data because there can be a big delay from feed generation to feed load. If we know when the feed is loaded, we can create the feed right before Setting a specific time for importing XML files on an e-commerce website's recommendations block is crucial for ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of product recommendations. Here's why:Freshness of Data: By setting a specific time for importing XML files, the system ensures that the latest updates from suppliers or product databases are included in the recommendations. This freshness of data is essential for providing customers with up-to-date information about products available for purchase.Relevance to Customers: Customers expect relevant recommendations based on their current interests and preferences. Importing XML files at specific times allows the system to incorporate the most recent data, thereby increasing the relevance of product recommendations. This relevance enhances the overall user experience and increases the likelihood of conversion.Competitive Advantage: In the highly competitive e-commerce landscape, staying ahead with the latest products and offerings is crucial. By importing XML files at specific times, the e-commerce website can ensure that its recommendations feature showcases the newest products, giving it a competitive edge over other platforms that may not update their recommendations as frequently.Accurate Inventory Management: Setting a specific time for importing XML files also aids in accurate inventory management. By regularly updating product information, including availability and pricing, the system can prevent recommending out-of-stock items or displaying outdated prices, which can lead to customer frustration and loss of sales.Optimized Performance: Importing XML files at specific times allows for better resource allocation and system performance optimization. By scheduling imports during off-peak hours or times of low website traffic, the system can minimize disruption to the user experience while ensuring that recommendations are continuously updated and available when customers visit the website.In conclusion, setting a specific time for importing XML files is essential for maintaining the freshness, relevance, and accuracy of product recommendations on an e-commerce website. By prioritizing timely updates, the platform can provide customers with a superior shopping experience, gain a competitive advantage, and drive increased sales and customer satisfaction.

Title: Barrier-free accessibility
Details: Pain Point: From mid-2025, websites and apps will be legally required to be barrier-free. This is regulated by the Barrier-Free Accessibility Strengthening Act (BFSG). The Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) implements the EU directive of the European Accessibility Act (EAA) so that standardised rules on accessibility apply throughout Europe. The regulations are based on the European standard EN 301 549, which in turn is largely based on the international guidelines for accessible web content (WCAG). e.g. sufficient contrast between foreground and background colour, links and buttons operable via the keyboard, screen reader compatibility of a website, etc. Even if the website offers this accessibility on its live site, there is still a risk that the variant of an experiment or personalisation will not fulfil it. Such a design can have legal consequences and penalties. Solution: There are various features in Kameleoon that check for accessibility when changes are made. The contrast check of colours in new editors is a first step and a good example of this. The customer wants more AI in the Graphic Editor. There is currently support for the barrier-free accessibility of headings, for example. One suggestion is that the AI should support where it is best to place the element. A possible suggestion is that the place where the element is best placed is highlighted in color. great differentiators with enterprise groups.

Details: We implemented Outlier Detection with Winsorization, using the revenue value fo filter out some data points we could do the same but by analysing the number of visits\/conversions of some users to filter them would be great for quantity per item, items per order, which don't include revenue In our day-to-day experimentation revenue is for sure the biggest usecase for outliers. Client : Sandvikemail: patrik.matell_c@sandvik.comNeed: be able to apply outliers to goals even if it's not related to revenueThanks-- Marie LemaireSenior Customer Success ManagerTel. +33 6 76 78 26 58www.kameleoon.comLynton House L7-12 Tavistock SquareWC1H 9LT London Our busniess operates in a context with some really massive customers, causeing many non-binary metrics to be unrealiable and frequent spikes when looking at graphs We have some distributors on our site. Title: AI suggestions - Unified text improvements
Details: # Statement** Currently, textual improvement suggestions are generated on a per-page basis for product pages, which can lead to redundant efforts when multiple pages contain similar or identical content needing revision. This approach can be inefficient and lacks a quantitative dimension to help prioritize which changes are most impactful. ### **Feature Principle** When identical or very similar text improvements are detected across multiple pages \(for instance, dozens of pages sharing the same snippet\), the system should offer a single consolidated solution for all those pages, with two possible approaches: 1. **LLM-Driven \(Automatic\)**: The LLM automatically selects the best improvement proposal based on context and text quality across those pages. 1. **User-Driven \(Tabular View\)**: A table displays different potential improvements, allowing the user to choose the most appropriate one based on quantitative criteria such as: - **Readability Score** \(e.g., Flesch-Kincaid\) - **SEO Impact Estimation** \(e.g., presence of relevant keywords\) - **Estimated Conversion Rate** \(if available, based on historical data or industry benchmarks\) - **Contextual Relevance** \(a rating of how well the text aligns with the pages intent and best writing practices\) #### **Quantitative Data to Include** - **Frequency of Occurrence**: The number of pages containing the text snippet to justify a single consolidated proposal. - **Comparative Analysis**: Evaluation of different proposals regarding readability, SEO potential, and historical performance. - **User Engagement Impact**: Potential effect of the changes on metrics like time on page or bounce rate. ### **Expected Impact** - **Reduced Redundancy**: Centralized management of similar text improvements across multiple pages, ensuring a more consistent user experience. - **Increased Relevance**: Quantitative data helps users make more informed decisions about which improvements to apply. - **Productivity Gains**: Users can swiftly apply the best suggestions to multiple pages without addressing each page individually.

Title: Custom Bucketing Key
Details: A **custom bucketing key** will allow you to control how users are consistently assigned to variations based on a user-defined identifier rather than the default one \(visitor code\). This is especially useful when your customers such as agencies \(or certain applications\) need to group users differently than the default logic for example, by account ID, session ID, device ID, or any other relevant key in your business logic. By using a custom bucketing key, you ensure that the same entity \(e.g., a company or group\) always gets the same variation, even if individual users change or switch devices. Its also helpful in B2B contexts where features should be rolled out at the **account level**, not the user level. This flexibility gives you greater targeting precision, consistency, and control in your rollouts and experiments.
